entities.name: Alí ibn al-Fadl al-Qarmatí
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: ʿAlī ibn al-Faḍl al-Jayshānī was a senior Isma'ili missionary from Yemen. In cooperation with Ibn Hawshab, he established the Isma'ili creed in his home country and conquered much of it in the 890s and 900s in the name of the hidden Isma'ili imam, Abdallah al-Mahdi Billah. After the establishment of the Fatimid Caliphate in Ifriqiya in 909, and the public proclamation of al-Mahdi Billah as caliph, Ibn al-Fadl denounced al-Mahdi as false, and instead declared himself to be the awaited messiah. His erstwhile colleague, Ibn Hawshab, refused to follow him, so Ibn al-Fadl turned against him and forced him to capitulate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alí ibn al-Fadl al-Qarmatí's actions led to the establishment of the Isma'ili creed in Yemen and his conquests in the region, which had significant regional impact. His denunciation of Abdallah al-Mahdi Billah as false caliph also influenced the Fatimid Caliphate's trajectory.
